comments.content:
`isAheadOf` can return `true` through its code branch even when `snapshotLatestVersion` is null, and the assignment then writes `null` over an already-recorded skip. The old guard `!snapshotLatestVersion.isNullOrBlank()` prevented exactly this, but it was dropped when the comparison moved into the helper (the helper only validates a non-blank candidate tag in its tag-fallback branch, not in the code branch).

This state is reachable, not theoretical: `clearUpdateMetadata` nulls `latestVersion`/`latestVersionCode` together while keeping `skippedReleaseTag`; a subsequent `updateAppVersion` for an older build has `latestStillNewer == false`, so line 524 repopulates `latestVersionCode = newVersionCode (> 0)` while `latestVersion` stays null. A second step-back then hits `isAheadOf(null, newTag, oldCode > 0, olderCode > 0)` -> `true` and clobbers the user's skip to null. Since `getAppsWithSkippedReleaseTag`/`checkForUpdates` rely on this field, a declined release can silently reappear in the Skipped Updates screen and be re-advertised.

Restore the non-blank requirement for the skip-recording path.

comments.content: The gate assumes `isPendingInstall` means "the file was only parked, the install never ran". That is not how the flag is used today: on Android the ordinary install flow returns `InstallOutcome.DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM` (AndroidInstaller.install), `saveInstalledAppToDatabase` maps any non-`COMPLETED` outcome to `isPending = true` (DetailsViewModel.kt:2105), and that value is forwarded here. Likewise `PackageEventReceiver.onPackageInstalled` calls `updateAppVersion(...)` without overriding the interface default `isPendingInstall = true` (InstalledAppsRepository.kt:42) when it confirms a real install. So this condition also suppresses the `skippedReleaseTag` rewrite for installs the user actually ran (the common Android case), which re-advertises the release they deliberately stepped away from — the behaviour the method exists to prevent. If the intent is only to exclude parked files, keying on a dedicated signal (e.g. the parked-file state) rather than `isPendingInstall` would be more precise.
